behavior: Mission signal event still sets original interrupted Event; adds best-effort immutable per-event JSON receipts.
No decision, candidate, score, stop threshold, timeout or actuator cleanup ordering change. Optional helper callbacks only occur after existing before/after verification returns.
Observer catches TERM/INT and forwards at most one SIGINT to existing mission PID, then keeps passive rings alive while waiting for mission cleanup; no new session/group or actuator ownership.
Milestone files use exclusive creation, flush/fsync; recording exceptions are swallowed and exposed in root lifecycle_recording_errors when root result survives.
supervisor_started/observer_started and every receipt record pid,ppid,pgid,sid; metadata only.
risks: Synchronous diagnostic filesystem I/O adds small latency and can block on a hung filesystem; no timing equivalence claim.
SIGKILL, host loss or outer executor escalation cannot be handled; same-group TERM still reaches descendants independently. Receipts identify received signal, not sender.
Interrupted write may leave a partial diagnostic file; a root_saved marker means the existing save call returned, not independent disk durability certification.
Observer can wait indefinitely if a signalled mission hangs; it deliberately adds no new kill authority or shutdown deadline. Existing exception-path finally wait20s is retained.
Dry tests exercise actual observer main using mocked ROS, CAN and mission process; actual OS signals are separately exercised in pure-helper subprocess. No live actuator/process-tree test performed.
original_logs: Prior full01 failure and report files were not modified.
deployment: No service restart or robot trial executed; root owns next execution.
review_correction: Root caught receive callback name shadowing in initial patch; fixed to receive_signal before any physical run. Prior pure-helper test was insufficient; actual-main regression and negative mutation check now added.
